speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin lesion on your chest; could you tell me how long it has been there and if it is itchy, painful, or changing in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your age, the two-month duration, and the reported increase in size, is this lesion a new growth or did you notice something change in an existing mole? Also, please describe its color and if it has any irregular borders.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; to further characterize this new growth, is the surface of the lesion smooth, scaly, or ulcerated, and do you notice any hair growth within or around it? Additionally, regarding your history of diabetes, have you noticed any other areas of skin breakdown or non-healing wounds recently?

REQUEST TEST: Full Body Skin Exam & Dermoscopy of lesion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent measurements show normal readings, but I need to rely on the visual inspection. Does the Full Body Skin Exam reveal a lesion with an uneven border, varied colors, or a diameter larger than 6mm? I am also requesting the images from the exam to better assess the morphology. REQUEST IMAGES: Full Body Skin Exam & Dermoscopy.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, glaucoma Social history: Smokes 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the last 40 years, drinks two to three beers on weekends

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's history of heavy smoking and diabetes increases the suspicion for malignancy, but I need to know if you have noticed any bleeding, crusting, or a "stuck-on" appearance to the lesion. Are there any changes in your vision related to your glaucoma that might correlate with this chest issue?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of chest lesion.
REQUEST IMAGES: Full Body Skin Exam & Dermoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 75 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: A single, partly elevated lesion on the chest showing asymmetry, irregular borders, varied color, and a diameter larger than 6mm; palpation reveals a firm lesion that does not change form on pinching. Biopsy: Histopathology shows atypical melanocytes infiltrating the epidermis and dermis, confirming the diagnosis of malignant melanoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Melanoma.

The biopsy results confirm the presence of atypical melanocytes infiltrating the epidermis and dermis, which is diagnostic for malignant melanoma. Given the history of significant risk factors including heavy smoking, diabetes, and a lesion with asymmetry and irregular borders, immediate surgical excision is indicated.
